title: Looking at a shelf piece mid-throw leaves your wet clay rendered as a fired, glazed pot
repro: Sit at the wheel and throw for a while (ST.THROW). Esc -> The shelf -> tap a piece -> Back -> Back -> Back to work. dressPot has set uFired/uBisque/uVitrified to 1 and installed the shelf piece's glaze via applyFireResult. _updateThrow rewrites uWet and uSlip every frame (game.js:1460-1461) but never touches uFired, uBisque or uVitrified — those are reset only in startThrow (game.js:1152-1155) and partially in startGlaze (1748-1749, which never resets uVitrified at all). So the soft clay under your hand goes on being drawn as a fired, vitrified, glazed pot for the rest of throwing and trimming

title: The very first commission asks for 500 g of clay and the weight slider will not go below 600
repro: Start a new game. Commission c1 ('Something To Drink From', require: { form: 'cup', minH: 8, maxH: 14, maxWall: 0.95 }) is the first brief anyone sees. showBrief does `this.mass = suggestedMass(c.require)` (game.js:1032), which returns 500. The label prints '500 g' but the range input clamps its own value to its min, so the thumb sits pinned at the far left reading 600 — the number and the control disagree on the first screen of the game. Touch the slider once and this.mass jumps to at least 600 and the 500 g the designer weighed out can never be dialled back. suggestedMass clamps to [250, 320

repro: this._newUnlocks is assigned ONLY inside the `r.accepted && !procedural` branch, and showReport reads it unconditionally at game.js:2539 `const unl = this._newUnlocks ?? [];`. Pass the commission that unlocks Tenmoku and Blackhill (lore.js:226 `unlocks: { glaze: 'tenmoku', body: 'blackhill' }`) — the report correctly shows 'New in the shed: Tenmoku · Blackhill'. Now fail the next commission (score under 40, or have it destroyed in the kiln, so accepted is false). _applyResults skips the whole branch, _newUnlocks still holds ['Tenmoku','Blackhill'], and the failure report proudly announces 'New

title: 'Dipped to N%' prints the fraction of the pot that stayed OUT of the bucket
repro: The two `??` defaults on the same variable, two lines apart, are complements of each other — 0.2 and 0.8 — which is only consistent if one of the two expressions is measuring the opposite quantity from the other. _dipFrac is the glaze LINE as a fraction of height measured up from the foot (`const frac = clamp01(this.tool.y / Math.max(1, c.height))`, game.js:2028), and GlazeField.dip(depthFrac) glazes everything above `top * (1 - depthFrac)` — so passing 1 - _dipFrac correctly glazes from the line up to the rim, i.e. the coverage is 1 - _dipFrac. title: Pressing Enter while the kiln is opening re-opens the results card a second later
repro: openKiln sets state = ST.REVEAL and schedules showReport 1500 ms later, with no way to cancel it, while advance() also routes ST.REVEAL to showReport (game.js:2798-2799) and Enter is unguarded (game.js:489 `if (k === 'Enter') { e.preventDefault(); this.advance(); return; }`; advance's only guard is `if (this.hud.overlayOpen) return`, and no overlay is open during those 1500 ms). Press Enter as soon as the kiln opens: the card appears with the chime and the score bars animating out. 1.5 s later the pending timeout fires showReport again — openOverlay does `this.ovInner.innerHTML = html` (hud.js

title: Portrait-iPad coach line is squeezed to a ~110px column of single words whenever the side panel is open
repro: iPad in portrait (834 CSS px wide), glaze stage. The shelf (#context) is up, so Hud._measure publishes --side-w = innerWidth - context.left. #coach is centred between left:0 and right:0, so it subtracts that reach TWICE even though there is only one panel (the commission is display:none below 900px). The one-line instruction ("Hold the left button on the clay and move your hand up and down the side...") becomes a narrow tower of one or two words per line standing between the tool belt and the pot.

title: Commission requirements are clipped off the bottom of a panel that cannot be scrolled
repro: Take a brief with many requirements (lore.js has one with 8: form, body, glaze, atmos, minH, maxH, minD, maxWall; six others have 6) on a short window. The requirement lines run past the bottom edge of #commission and are cut. Nothing can be done about it: the panel is overflow:hidden, so there is no wheel scroll, no drag, no scrollbar — and the fade mask added at line 1019 ('text that fades out is text that continues') advertises exactly the scrolling that overflow:hidden forbids, as does the -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch next to it. The player is then graded against a requirement the inte

title: The target silhouette is drawn 43% too short on any window under 760px tall, so the shape you are told to match is the wrong shape
repro: Play on an iPad in landscape (the CSS itself measures that viewport as 1194x675) or any window <=760px tall. The commission panel draws the asked-for profile as a dashed outline and your pot over it. Because #silho has width:100% and height:auto, capping max-height does NOT preserve the aspect ratio (CSS 2.1 10.4: with width specified and height auto, a max-height violation is resolved by using max-height as the height) — the canvas bitmap is squashed vertically. A tall jar is drawn as a squat bowl, and 'match the dashed outline on the left' is coaching the player toward the wrong proportions.

title:
Hiding the glaze type label reclaims no height at all, because the

repro:
Glaze stage on any screen <=900px in either dimension (both iPad orientations). style.css:1163 sets '.glaze .gt{display:none}' with the comment 'Dropping it makes every item one line instead of two and the whole shelf fits with room to spare'. It does not: display:none removes the label but the
before it still generates an empty line box, so each bucket stays two lines tall. The shelf still overflows and the player still has to scroll a list that was supposed to fit — having lost the family label for nothing.

title: The on-device diagnostic panel inherits pointer-events:none, so it can never be scrolled
repro: Tap the day counter four times on the iPad to open #diag (the readout built because the player has no web inspector). It is appended into #hud (dev/diag.js:56), and #hud is pointer-events:none (line 175) with auto restored only for '.panel, nav, button, .clickable' (line 177). #diag is a plain div matching none of those, so it computes to pointer-events:none: the wheel does nothing over it, a finger does nothing over it, and the -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch on line 996 is decoration. title: #hud.viewing hides two elements that do not exist: the tool belt and the bottom bar stay on screen over a finished piece
repro: During a day, open the menu, go to the gallery, tap a piece. game.js:2647 adds .viewing to #hud, and the comment says 'the room stays, the workbench does not'. #context and #commission do go (their ids are right). But the ids in index.html are #tools (line 74) and #hud-bottom (line 83) — there is no #toolbar and no #bottom-bar anywhere in the document — so the six glaze tool buttons and the whole bottom bar with the key hints and the Continue button stay lit up across the bottom of the shot of your finished pot.

title: The one-column glaze shelf rule is dead: a later three-column rule wins on narrow AND short windows
repro: A window that is both narrow and short — a phone in portrait, or a 600x600 desktop window. Line 1173's '@media (max-height: 680px){ .glaze-list{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr 1fr} }' has the same specificity and comes later, so the deliberate 'below this there is genuinely no room for two columns' rule never fires. You get three columns in a panel that is 40vw wide, and the glaze names are ellipsised down to one or two characters.

title: The clearcoat patch never applies — onBeforeCompile runs before three resolves #include, so material.clearcoat is a flat per-material value and S.clear/S.clearRough are computed and thrown away
repro: Glaze a piece so part of it is left bare (wipe the foot, or use wax resist), or pick a dry/matt glaze, and fire it. In the REVEAL the bare foot and the matt glaze carry exactly the same hard glass highlight as a glossy glaze, and the highlight tracks the overhead lamp as you orbit. The shader computes the correct per-pixel answer (S.clear = 0 on bare clay, 0 on dryG) at potMaterial.js:456 and it never reaches the renderer. title: The clay wrap-lighting and warm-transmission replacements are silent no-ops for the same reason — clayWrap 0.55 and the rawNL tint never reach the compiled shader
repro: Throw a pot and orbit until the lamp is off to one side. The terminator on the wall of the pot is a hard Lambert edge — light on one side of it, nothing on the other — which is exactly the 'surface is hard' cue the comment two lines above says was removed. There is also no warm pigment carried past the terminator. Confirmed by running mat.onBeforeCompile() against THREE.ShaderLib.physical: neither 'clayWrap' nor 'rawNL' appears anywhere in the patched fragment shader.

title: Lifting one of three fingers slams the camera: goalRadius 58 -> 16, or 94 degrees of azimuth in one event
repro: iPad, any room. Rest three fingers on the canvas (thumb + two, or a palm-edge finger joining a pinch — common on a tablet). Move them enough to arm the arbiter. Now lift one of the two that landed FIRST, leaving two down. On the very next pointermove — a 1px twitch is enough — the camera either snaps to the closest allowed radius (pinch was classified 'zoom') or the whole studio spins about a quarter turn (classified 'drag'). Same thing happens if iPadOS sends pointercancel for one finger instead of pointerup: cancel routes through the same `up` at game.js:426-446.

title: During the firing the hint says SCROLL zoom, but scrolling spins the wheel motor up instead
repro: Desktop. Set a kiln schedule, click 'Light the kiln'. The key-hint bar still reads 'DRAG sliders · RMB orbit · SCROLL zoom · ENTER light it' — lightKiln() at game.js:2237 sets state = ST.FIRING and never calls setKeyHints (there are only four call sites in the whole file: 1195, 1720, 1765, 2125). Now scroll up to zoom in on the kiln. Nothing zooms. Instead the wheel motor audibly spins up behind the kiln roar, with no wheel visible anywhere — the studio is told omega:0 during FIRING (game.js:1261) but the audio mixer is handed this.omega unconditionally (game.js:1300). repro: Throwing room, default settings (save.js:57 has assist:true), default tool (hands). Drag the WHEEL bar — the pedal wired up at hud.js:106-121 — all the way to the right. repro: iPad, throwing room. Try to drag the WHEEL bar to change the speed. It is 7 CSS px tall — the only interactive gauge in the game, and the ONLY one made SHORTER than the read-only ones (.gauge .bar is height:12px at style.css:279). `grep -n pedal src/ui/style.css` returns exactly three hits, 287/291/292, none of them inside a @media (pointer:coarse) block; the coarse block at style.css:804-819 goes out of its way to bump .tool to 60x66, .btn padding to 1.15em/1.7em, and input[type=range] to height:34px with 26px thumbs. title: step() runs three full-strength box blurs per frame with no dt, so the pot heals itself twice as fast on a 120 Hz screen
repro: Knock the rim off true so there is one visible lump, take the hand off the clay entirely and let the wheel turn for ten seconds. On a 120 Hz iPad the lump is 0.010 cm; on a 60 Hz display it is 0.014 cm; at 30 fps it is 0.020 cm. The pot repairs itself at whatever rate the screen refreshes, with no input at all — and the clay softens and equalises at that same rate, so plasticity under the hand differs by device.

title: open() is the one smoothing call that forgets the `amount` argument, so it blurs the bore outright every frame
repro: Press down into the middle of a fresh lump and hold. The shoulder where the floor turns into the wall softens upward at a rate set by the refresh rate rather than by how long or how hard you pressed. The same opening stroke leaves a measurably different floor on a 120 Hz iPad than on a 60 Hz desktop.

title: _smoothProfile never smooths the inner wall — the branch that would is unreachable
repro: Cut a step into the wall with a jerky stroke, then hold the rib on it. The outer silhouette comes clean; the bore keeps the step. Grep confirms it: `grep -n '_smoothProfile' src/sim/clay.js` gives 376, 707, 787, 912 — every caller passes 0.

title: One codex fragment can never be unlocked — stats.drowned is never incremented anywhere
repro: `grep -rn drowned src/` returns exactly two hits in the whole codebase: this predicate, and `drowned: 0` in the blankSave initializer (save.js:58). Nothing ever writes it — not clay.js (which tracks stats.waterUsed but never reports it up), not _updateThrow, not _collapse. The other six CODEX predicates all read counters that are written (stats.centred at game.js:1598, stats.collapses at 1683, firings at 1753, crazed at 2469/2482, best at 2468). repro: quickWater is set only in _onKey (game.js:509, `if (this.state === ST.THROW) { this.quickWater = true; }` — the SPACE key advertised as 'SPACE water' in the key hints). 'water' : this.toolId;`) and then clears it at game.js:1451 (`this.quickWater = false;`). Only afterwards, at game.js:1314, does audio.update read it — by which time it is unconditionally false. title: The TOUCH block is no longer last: .glaze's coarse-pointer padding is dead on both iPad orientations
repro: This is the third occurrence of the fault whose fix the file documents twice ('THIS BLOCK MUST STAY AT THE END OF THE FILE'). Two blocks have since been appended after @media (pointer:coarse): line 1161 '@media (max-height: 900px), (max-width: 900px){ .glaze{padding:.2em .4em} }' and line 1172 '@media (max-height: 680px){ .glaze{...padding:.16em .3em} }'. Equal specificity, later wins — and an iPad matches the 900px block in BOTH orientations (834 wide in portrait, 834 tall in landscape). So the one enlargement made for fingers on the control the whole glazing phase runs through never applies

title: The Hide-panels button — the control added for the iPad complaint — is a 31px touch target
repro: On the iPad, the button that folds the panels away sits in the bottom-right corner. Its own stylesheet declares 44px as the floor for a thumb ('44px is the size everyone converged on', line 803), and the coarse-pointer bump here takes it to 31px. Its contents are an 11px icon box and an 11px/1 line of type, so the padding is all there is.

title: S.irid is computed every frame and never read; mat.iridescence is never set, so the iridescence path the comment claims to force is never compiled
repro: Fire an oil-spot, hematite or any metallic glaze (uSlotQ.z / uSlotR.x / uSlotS.z > 0). The shader raises S.irid for exactly those pixels and nothing consumes it — the glaze reads as flat metal-tinted colour with no thin-film shift. Verified by running onBeforeCompile: 'celIrid' occurs exactly once in the patched fragment shader, which is its own declaration at potMaterial.js:619 ('float celIrid = S.irid;'). There is no .replace() anywhere in the file that writes material.iridescence.

title: Studio._mat() silently drops every normalMap and roughnessMap handed to it, so all six tuned normalScale values in the room are dead
repro: Look at the sponge on the bench. studio.js:558-562 builds it with clothMaps and normalScale (2.2, 2.2) under a comment saying 'The cloth maps give it a tooth' — it has no tooth, it is a flat-shaded lumpy blob. Same for the floor (normalScale 0.8, line 134), the plaster walls (1.1, line 147), the wheel head (0.45, line 302), the bucket (0.7, line 582) and the kiln bricks (1.15, line 776). _mat reads only maps.map from its first argument; normalMap and roughnessMap are passed in that same first argument at every call site and never copied onto the material. normalScale arrives via ...o and three

title: The flywheel turns at 0.42x the wheel head despite a rigid shaft drawn between them
repro: Kick the wheel up to speed and crouch (drag down until the splash pan fades) so both the head and the flywheel are in frame. The three spokes on the flywheel visibly lag the head's texture. studio.js:434-439 builds a solid CylinderGeometry(2.6, 3.6, 40) shaft joining the two, and studio.js:428 a stretcher ring — there is no gearing anywhere in the model, so a kick wheel's flywheel and head are on one shaft at 1:1. No comment in the file defends the 0.42, and every other deliberate deviation here is commented at length.

title: The two-finger banding-wheel flick uses a magic *22 where the mouse path divides by real elapsed time
repro: Glaze room. Flick the pot with a right-button mouse drag at a moderate speed and let go — it coasts about 83 degrees. Do the same flick with two fingers on the iPad and it coasts 40 degrees on a 60Hz iPad, 20 degrees on a 120Hz iPad Pro. Same gesture, same speed, three different amounts of coast, and the tablet is always the weakest. Directly above it, game.js:259-262 solves exactly this for the mouse and the comment at game.js:242-249 explains why per-event deltas without elapsed time are wrong; the touch branch reintroduces it.

title: A mouse pointercancel leaves pointer.right stuck true — the camera then orbits with no button held
repro: Desktop. Hold the right button and drag to orbit. If a pointercancel is dispatched for that pointer instead of a pointerup — the browser starting a native drag, the OS taking the pointer — the branch that clears pointer.right never runs, because the Pointer Events spec sets button to -1 on pointercancel (buttons 0), not to 2. Control falls to game.js:442-443, which clears pointer.down (already false) and fires a phantom _onRelease().
